business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light services model with a dual execution framework rather than owned manufacturing. Booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to subcontractors while design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations; all subcontractors are directly hired and managed by the Company and all subcontracted work is carried out under its active guidance and on-ground supervision, with supervisors physically present on-site for the full duration of the project. Both partial and full subcontracting models are used, and the Company also takes on subcontracted work from other firms. The outsourcing model runs a formal two-step process (vendor screening - define project requirements, identify potential vendors, pre-screening checklist covering GST/PAN and financial stability, RFP/RFQ, proposal evaluation, vendor interviews, due diligence and background checks including litigation/blacklisting, final selection and contracting, onboarding and governance; then project execution - project management tools, milestone work plan, daily status calls and on-site monitoring, final delivery and handover). The in-house model covers material requirement definition (plywood, commercial ply, nylon carpet rolls and other construction/finish items), vendor shortlisting, RFQ, quotation evaluation, purchase order issue, material delivery and inspection, payment processing and inventory recordkeeping. Revenue by execution mode (% of total revenue): Subcontract 90.89% / 92.11% / 75.48% / 64.40% and In-house 9.11% / 7.89% / 24.52% / 35.60% for the period ended Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23. Vendor and execution metrics (not cumulative), Feb 28, 2026 / FY25 / FY24 / FY23: total active subcontractors globally (domestic and international) 53 / 36 / 29 / 22; projects executed with international local allies 125 / 69 / 49 / 20; projects executed domestically 307 / 312 / 207 / 205; total booths delivered globally 432 / 381 / 256 / 225; total repeat clients 63 / 27 / 28 / 48; average project turnaround time 3 to 30 days in every period. The Company states it does not own fabrication machinery or permanent event spaces and instead rents godowns, fabrication equipment, raw materials and temporary project sites project-by-project; materials are sourced locally in overseas markets to reduce logistics dependencies. Risk factors disclose that there are no executed registered formal arrangements with the outsourced subcontractors governing specifications, quality standards, sales estimates or packaging, and that foreign outsourcing adds FX, cross-border regulatory, geopolitical and logistical exposure. Registered office and both godowns are on leasehold premises. International client base grew 245% over the last three years, from 20 to 69 international clients; total booths delivered globally grew at a stated CAGR of 30.13% from FY23 to FY25.

M NO : 138235W'; and 'Priyanka Lad' is separated from her designation 'Chief Finance Officer'. A second, blank 'UDIN :' field appears under the Company Secretary's membership number.

No date of cessation is recorded for any director in the last three years, and no ceased officer is disclosed anywhere in the routed text - hence kmp_attrition is omitted rather than populated.

Bonus-issue arithmetic does not reconcile: the EPS note states 'a resolution on 25th July 2025 for a bonus issue. 85,30,804 bonus shares were issued to each shareholder at a ratio of 11:34.' Pre-bonus capital of Rs. 276.00 lakh at March 31, 2025 implies 27,60,000 shares; a 34-for-11 issue on that base would be 85,30,909 shares (105 more than stated), and the ratio as literally written (11 new for 34 held) would produce only 8,92,941 shares. The post-bonus total of 1,12,90,804 shares is not divisible in the stated ratio. The earlier note is similarly inverted: 'a resolution on 04th January 2024 for a bonus issue. 1000000 bonus shares were issued to each shareholder at a ratio of 1:100' against a pre-bonus base of 10,000 shares (Rs. 1.00 lakh capital) is a 100-for-1 issue, not 1:100.

EPS share-count basis is internally inconsistent across periods: shares outstanding at year end are 0.10 lakh (FY2023), 19.29 lakh (FY2024), 27.60 lakh (FY2025) and 112.91 lakh (11M FY2026), while the weighted average used is 95.41 / 95.51 / 103.83 / 112.91 lakh. The FY2023 weighted average exceeds the year-end count by roughly 954x. The retrospective bonus adjustment is not explained in the routed text, and the resulting series shows EPS falling from 6.09 (FY2025) to 5.72 (11M FY2026) despite higher absolute profit.

Note 15 (Restated Other current Assets) carries a fifth column dated 31-03-2022 (totalling 166.15) that lies outside the restated reporting period (February 28, 2026 and FY2025/FY2024/FY2023) and outside the auditor's examination scope; the same stray column appears on the Note 14 fragment. Note 15 also introduces a 'Pre IPO Expenses' asset of 42.92 (11M FY2026) and 5.56 (FY2025) carried within Other current assets rather than deferred or written off, with no accounting policy for it in the routed text.

Trade payables ageing rows are incomplete: the 'Due to Micro Enterprises & small enterprises' line carries only three dashes against four period columns and no note number, and the ageing captions ('Outstanding for period from due date of payment on Feb 28th 2026' / 'FY 24-25' / 'FY 23-24' / 'FY 22-23') appear detached from any values, so no MSME ageing bucket is attributable.

Profile-versus-record inconsistencies in 'Our Management': Prathamesh Shantaram Pusalkar is described as having 'more than 7 years of experience' while the same paragraph records him establishing the Propshop proprietary venture in 2013 (about 13 years) and holding prior roles at Reliance Retail and Meroform before that. Shreyas Shrikant Rumade is described as 'associated with company since inception' and as having overseen projects 'since the Company's inception', yet the Company was incorporated on August 22, 2019 and his 'Period of Directorship' is stated as 'Since June 12, 2024'.

Employment-history gap in an Independent Director's profile: Bhavesh Rameshkumar Jain's listed roles run July 2007 - June 2009 (Equant), June 2009 - August 2010 (ABS India), then March 2012 - November 2015 (Union Bank of India), leaving August 2010 to March 2012 unaccounted, and October 2024 to his appointment on March 24, 2025 unaccounted. The same profile states 'more than 12 years of experience' against a career starting in 2007 (about 19 years).

Post-Offer shareholding percentages for all three shareholding directors are placeholders '[.]' in the shareholding-of-directors table, and the post-Offer paid-up capital of Rs. 1,463.08 lakh is footnoted '*Subject to basis of allotment' - i.e. still subject to a future determination as at the date of the Red Herring Prospectus.

The Offer itself was authorised by the Board 'subject to the approval of the shareholders of the Company under Section 62(1)(c)'; that approval was subsequently obtained at the EGM of July 13, 2026. Borrowing powers up to Rs. 2,500 lakh under Section 180(1)(c) rest on a shareholders' special resolution of May 08, 2025.

Related-party disclosure in 'Our Management' and 'Our Promoters' is by cross-reference only ('Except as stated under Note 24 - Related Party Disclosures ... on page 245'); the quantum is carried solely in the Restated Financial Statements notes, and the routed 'RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS (recovered by RPT-table content signature)' block is what supplied every figure in the rpts array. The 'Summary of Related Party Transactions' chapter on page 76, referenced repeatedly, is not present in the routed text.

No KMP appointment dates are disclosed anywhere in the routed text for the Chief Financial Officer or the Company Secretary; the 'since' field is therefore omitted for both rather than inferred from the first period in which their remuneration appears (FY2025).

The Company confirms it has no subsidiary or associate as on the date of the Red Herring Prospectus, so no director remuneration is paid or payable by any subsidiary or associate; it also confirms no contingent or deferred compensation payable to Directors, no bonus or profit-sharing plan for Directors, no service contracts providing termination benefits, and no change in control of the Company in the five years preceding the Red Herring Prospectus.

overview.business_model: The Company sells end-to-end exhibition booth services to corporate clients participating in trade fairs and expos: concept design and 3D visualization, project management, logistics, on-site supervision, fabrication, installation and post-event dismantling. Design and conceptualization are handled in-house and through project-based collaborations; booth fabrication and related services are outsourced to directly hired subcontractors working under the Company's guidance and on-ground supervision, under both partial and full subcontracting models. The Company also takes on subcontracted work from other firms. Revenue by execution method for the period ended February 28, 2026 was 90.89% subcontracted (Rs 5,436.02 lakhs) and 9.11% in-house (Rs 544.76 lakhs). Work is executed in India and, through local teams, in the United States, United Kingdom, Dubai, Germany, Spain and Singapore. Clients span Industrial Machinery & Equipment, Building Materials, Furnishing and Decor, Chemicals, Media & Entertainment, Healthcare and Cosmetics, and Food & Beverages.
